judgment.facts: Sanjeev Singhal and Shefali Varma entered into an agreement dated 17 January 2022 to sell land in Gadaipur, Delhi, for Rs. 22 crore, with completion dependent on family settlements affecting Varma’s title. Although some land was conveyed to Singhal’s nominee in 2022, the settlement concerning the Neeta Anand parcel did not occur by 31 March 2022; Varma perfected her title to that parcel through an exchange deed in May 2024. The court upheld the arbitrator’s findings that the contractual deadline applied to the remaining obligations and that Singhal had not proved continuous readiness and willingness to perform. Varma admitted retaining Rs. 97 lakh refundable to Singhal.
judgment.motive: No criminal motive was examined or established. The civil dispute concerned the purchaser’s attempt to enforce a property sale agreement and the seller’s contention that her remaining contractual obligations had lapsed.
judgment.trigger: After learning that Varma had acquired title to the Neeta Anand parcel in May 2024, Singhal demanded completion of the remaining sale. Her failure to respond to his demand letters led him to invoke arbitration.
judgment.court_reasoning: The court upheld the arbitrator’s reading of Clauses 6 and 7 together, applying the 31 March 2022 deadline to the outstanding conveyance obligations; subsequent dealings concerning the co-ownership parcel did not establish revival of obligations concerning the Neeta Anand parcel. It also upheld the finding that Singhal had not proved continuous readiness and willingness, including transaction-specific financial capacity, under Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act. The arbitrator had addressed the material issues and correctly rejected a freestanding hardship-based discretion under the pre-2018 specific-performance regime. Because the award reflected a plausible contractual interpretation and evidentiary assessment, Section 34 did not permit reappreciation of evidence or substitution of the court’s own view.
judgment.outcome: The court dismissed O.M.P. 3/2026, the Section 34 challenge, with pending applications, and disposed of O.M.P.(I) 10/2026 seeking interim restraints as infructuous. The arbitral award remained undisturbed: specific performance and consequential declaratory and injunctive relief were refused, while Varma was directed to refund Rs. 97 lakh with 15% annual interest from 17 August 2022 to the award date, totaling Rs. 1,53,98,750. The award also provided 15% annual future interest on the outstanding balance if unpaid within 60 days and Rs. 25 lakh in costs to Singhal, with other fees and expenses shared equally. There was no criminal conviction or sentence.

timeline.description: The Neeta Anand family settlement had not occurred by the deadline. The court upheld the finding that Varma was discharged from further obligations under the agreement.
